title: Modeling, Derivation, and Automated Analysis of Branch Predictor Security Vulnerabilities
problem: Microarchitectural side-channel attacks targeting branch predictors exploit design flaws inadequately considered during architecture design. Current branch predictor architectures lack systematic frameworks to identify and analyze security vulnerabilities in the design phase.
motivation: These attacks threaten the security boundary of computer systems and users' security-critical data, requiring comprehensive automated analysis frameworks to catch vulnerabilities early.
method: A three-step modeling approach: (1) abstractly characterizes 19 branch predictor states and 53 operations, (2) applies symbolic execution to investigate three-step operation combinations and derive valid attack patterns, (3) evaluates 8 secure branch predictor designs and 4 hardware-based speculative execution countermeasures.
key_novelty: An automated symbolic execution-based framework that exhaustively explores and derives branch predictor attack patterns, discovering 89 novel attacks never previously considered.
contributions: Comprehensive abstract model of branch predictor security with 19 states and 53 operations
Symbolic execution-based automated framework for systematic attack pattern derivation and validation
Discovery of 156 valid attack patterns including 89 previously unknown attacks
Empirical validation demonstrating secure branch predictor designs outperform hardware-based speculative execution countermeasures
limitations: Practical deployment considerations and real-world performance overhead not discussed.
primary_theme: Automated branch predictor security vulnerability analysis
